_source: docs/design-bible.md: Room flavor and Oddities. Ships in the app by the DM's choice (Room generator defaults).

floors.title: the pilgrims' floor
details: Wax drippings and pressed flowers fill the cracks between columns, offerings to Thils.
Faint hymns hum through the stone, though no one is singing.
Chalk arrows from past tourists point in contradictory directions.
The basalt is warm to the touch, like stone left in the sun.
A brass tourist placard reads “Floor One: Mind the Shift,” half swallowed by fresh stone.
Hex tiles click softly underfoot, settling after every step.

floors.title: the expedition floor
details: A dented Archive survey beacon blinks a dead expedition's code.
A Pale Lodge contract tag is nailed to a column, its ink faded past reading.
A flickering strider replays a single step, over and over, then vanishes.
Abandoned gear lies scattered: a cracked lantern, a bedroll, one boot.
Voices argue around corners that aren't there about which way to go.
Scratched tallies on a wall count days, then stop.

floors.title: the gate floor
details: Gold-veined transit runes pulse along the floor slowly, like breathing.
The air hums at a pitch that makes teeth ache.
Shards of gate-glass hang in midair, turning slowly.
Thin veins of Quantum Basalt glint in the columns, too deep to pry loose.
Some columns are riveted struts engraved with stridegate schematics.
Static lifts hair and makes metal gear tick and spark.

floors.title: floor 4
details: Golden light falls from below, casting shadows upward.
Flowers bloom from the cracks, their petals folding shut in the light.
Birdsong plays backward and ends in silence.
The air smells of rain and honey, then for one breath, of ash.
Grass grows on the ceiling, and dew falls upward.
A painted meadow peels off a column from the inside out.

oddities: An item one of the players lost long ago, outside the dungeon, sits on a column top. Thils collects lost things.
An echo of a party member from a previous run walks past, mid-fight with something unseen.
A locked door with no keyhole stands alone in the middle of the room.
A column hums the name of a pilgrim who visited long ago.
The room is an exact copy of one from a previous run, down to the scuff marks.
A local's prayer to Thils is carved fresh into the floor, still dusty.
